determinism.accounting: byte scans, token parses, clause and literal checks, watch installation and movement, assignments, propagation queue operations, visits, deletion lookups, fallback transition, comparisons, and result construction consume deterministic counters checked before work or allocation can exceed a declared bound
determinism.canonicalization: CNF and certificate inputs use the exact versioned ASCII LF grammars in requires; replay results use closed sorted compact ASCII JSON with one trailing LF, full lowercase SHA-256 identities, fixed fields, and fixed semantic array or tuple order
determinism.identity: the result binds original canonical CNF bytes, original canonical certificate bytes, their full SHA-256 values, format and claim, checker implementation and contract, verdict, reason, diagnostic, authority, exactness, and all replay statistics
determinism.platform: behavior depends only on exact input bytes and declared CPython bytes, integer, tuple, dict, list, bytearray, dataclass, JSON, and SHA-256 semantics, never on locale, default encoding, clock, host, checkout, environment, installed solvers, scheduling, hash iteration, or filesystem state
determinism.streaming: line and token boundaries are determined only by exact byte offsets; splitting the internal scan at any byte boundary yields identical counters and result, while CRLF and unterminated records are rejected as noncanonical

effects.mutation: caller bytes are never mutated; all returned values own immutable exact fields and replay scratch state is local and discarded before return
effects.solver: none and no PySAT, Z3, SymPy, DPLL producer, Ramsey encoder, discovery producer, router, MCP, CLI, clock, filesystem, process, environment, randomness, dynamic import, or proof-assistant module is imported or executed

ensures: check_sat_certificate is total over ordinary Python objects and returns one immutable verified, refuted, invalid, unsupported, or exhausted SATReplayResult without converting malformed input, implementation defects, solver claims, timeouts, or partial work into checker authority.
A verified SAT result is issued only after the certificate CNF identity matches and every canonical CNF clause has at least one literal made true by the complete exact assignment.

A verified UNSAT result is issued only after every added DRUP lemma is reverse-unit-propagation implied by the accumulated formula and either the empty clause is derived or the final formula unit-propagates to conflict.

DRUP deletion removes the most recently added active exact canonical clause match when one exists and is a deterministic no-op otherwise; the checker may retain entailed deleted clauses and switch permanently to include-deleted propagation after a deletion-sensitive RUP miss because this is sound only inside the explicitly RUP-only format.

DRAT and genuine RAT-bearing evidence is never interpreted by the DRUP algorithm, never reaches the include-deleted fallback, and returns FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED with authority none until a separately contracted RAT checker exists.

Every verified result binds the exact CNF and certificate SHA-256 identities, claim, versioned format, checker identity, accepted contract identity, exact=true, complete deterministic replay statistics, stable diagnostic, and checker_attestation authority.
Refuted, invalid, unsupported, and exhausted results have authority none; no partial assignment, lemma, clause, watch state, conflict, statement, or producer assertion survives as checker authority.

SATReplayResult and its statistics have closed public constructors, frozen slots, final subclass behavior, exact scalar fields, blocked pickle reduction, identity-preserving safe copying, canonical result bytes, full result SHA-256, and complete recomputation at every validation or parse boundary.

CNF and certificate parsing scans bounded byte ranges incrementally by newline and token without constructing a whole proof line list or recursively parsing input; certificate identity is computed over the original exact bytes.

mathhead.drat and mathhead.discovery.rup_check preserve their documented legacy input and result shapes only through non-authoritative adapters that normalize into this canonical checker and translate its outcome without importing producer authority into mathhead.kernel.sat.

The implementation remains within the MH-030 dependency-minimal closure of at most twelve internal modules and nine approved standard-library roots with zero third-party, denied, dynamic-import, or effect roots.

epistemics.exhausted: the exact input is structurally supported but complete replay could not finish inside deterministic declared counters; no SAT or UNSAT authority is issued
epistemics.invalid: an input type, encoding, CNF grammar, certificate grammar, canonical form, identity, deletion, or result invariant is invalid; no mathematical claim is evaluated or retained
epistemics.refuted: a complete SAT assignment falsifies a clause or a supported DRUP record fails reverse unit propagation or closure, so the supplied certificate does not establish its claim
epistemics.unsupported: the certificate declares DRAT, RAT, an unknown format, or an unknown version outside this checker fragment; no statement is made about truth or falsity
epistemics.verified: the dependency-minimal checker exactly replayed a complete SAT assignment or supported RUP-only DRUP refutation and issued checker_attestation for the CNF claim

invariants: The only authoritative certificate formats are sat-assignment-v1 for SAT and drup-v1 for UNSAT; drat-v1 is recognized only to refuse RAT semantics explicitly.

Exact type checks apply at every boundary: bool is never an integer, Unicode text is never certificate bytes, zero is only a record terminator, literal magnitude is between one and 1000000, and decimal tokens have one canonical spelling.

Canonical CNF normalization is semantic and unique: literal order, clause order, duplicate removal, tautology removal, variable maximum, counts, ASCII spacing, LF framing, and trailing newline have one representation; adapters normalize legacy collections before checker replay and cannot claim authority for discarded raw bytes.
SAT assignments contain every declared variable exactly once in magnitude order, contain no unknown or duplicate variable, and verify only if every clause is satisfied.

Every DRUP addition is checked before insertion by assuming the complement of its unique literals and performing unit propagation to conflict over the current formula; tautological proof clauses are noncanonical and cannot exploit contradictory assumptions.

Two-watched-literal state retains exact active and deleted clause identities, never indexes variable zero, resets every temporary assignment after each lemma, treats empty and unit clauses explicitly, and uses deterministic clause, watch, trail, and replacement order.

Deletion is never a proof step, never grants authority, and cannot erase the retained identity or entailment status of an original clause or already verified lemma; include-deleted fallback is reachable only for the drup-v1 format.

A proof may verify without a final explicit empty record only when unit propagation on the final accumulated entailed formula derives conflict; arbitrary truncation that lacks this closure is refuted.

Input byte, record byte, variable, clause, literal, width, record, deletion, watch, assignment, propagation, visit, logical-step, and result-byte ceilings are checked before corresponding parsing, allocation, loop, or output work; exhaustion never returns a partial verified state.

Every in-memory or serialized result validation reruns check_sat_certificate on retained exact CNF and certificate bytes and requires structural equality of identities, claim, format, verdict, reason, diagnostic, authority, exactness, and counters.

Producer names, solver success, legacy verified booleans, elapsed time, result class names, object constructor history, private-looking fields, object.__new__, object.__setattr__, copying, pickling, subclassing, hashes without bytes, and compatibility adapters cannot mint checker_attestation.

The implementation imports only approved standard-library support and mathhead.kernel modules, carries exactly one top-level MH-C-SAT-REPLAY-001 ID and accepted SHA-256 binding, resolves the declared check_sat_certificate signature exactly, and imports no legacy checker or producer module.
raises: Ordinary wrong types, malformed or noncanonical CNF and certificate bytes, false claims, unsupported formats, and deterministic resource exhaustion return classified non-authoritative SATReplayResult values rather than escaping as validation exceptions.

SATReplayValidationError with kind type, encoding, schema, canonical, duplicate, identity, result, or budget is raised only by explicitly requested result validation, hashing, serialization, or parse boundaries receiving forged, stale, malformed, noncanonical, or over-budget result data.
PermissionError is raised for direct public construction of replay result and statistics classes, and TypeError is raised for subclass or pickle attempts.
MemoryError, KeyboardInterrupt, and SystemExit propagate and never yield a SATReplayResult, certificate identity, conflict claim, or mathematical authority.
requires: The accepted MH-C-WORKFLOW-001=99cfdf17371938af65c4203c02cbaac0bf73470e9fab59f7a6d62360fc0b7cca, MH-C-TRUST-BASE-001=2d2c23da4d3b167c5220c7548602f11403af7634031c438a8f61ac8e3e191456, MH-C-EVIDENCE-001=c68c20ca599cfdd7aabe9b85f2817c6c3f1a121289334136ff048768ee20c3b3, MH-C-CERTIFICATE-001=0a21aca8058fb5fc9900decb6dcd14e179c7a5171f7653ea965b5d34edd59740, and MH-C-KERNEL-CHECKER-002=1baf3b44734369fdb298609ad0230062686697a7198401d6fc53f161c70a678e govern the checker and producer separation.

cnf and certificate are exact bytes values no larger than 67108864 bytes each; text, bytearray, memoryview, streams, paths, iterators, and implicit coercions are rejected by the authoritative boundary.

Canonical CNF bytes are strict ASCII with LF only, begin with p mathhead-cnf 1 followed by exact nonnegative variable and clause counts, contain exactly that many newline-terminated clauses, and contain no blank, comment, trailing, CRLF, tab, leading-zero, plus-sign, or noncanonical whitespace bytes.

Each canonical CNF clause is one space-separated sequence of unique nonzero signed decimal literals in strictly increasing (absolute value, negative before positive) order followed by 0; complementary literals and duplicate clauses are forbidden, clauses are in lexicographic integer-tuple order, and the header variable count equals the greatest literal magnitude or zero.

A SAT certificate begins with p mathhead-sat-assignment 1 and the lowercase SHA-256 of the exact CNF bytes, followed by exactly one v record containing one sign choice for every variable from one through the declared maximum in magnitude order and a zero terminator.

A supported UNSAT certificate begins with p mathhead-drup 1 and the lowercase SHA-256 of the exact CNF bytes, followed by canonical a addition or d deletion clause records. A p mathhead-drat 1 header is a recognized but unsupported RAT-bearing format and unknown headers or versions are unsupported without mathematical authority.
The closed result envelope is governed by docs/contracts/schemas/sat-replay-result-v1.schema.json=e7bccaba76958f185a94d7570b5c65972a855dd99888c04269074491506ef242.
